articles.title: Liverpool come back to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in Champions League opener
articles.summary: Marcos Llorente gives Atleti an early lead but Liverpool strike back through Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister.
articles.body:
Alexis Mac Allister made his case for an improved Liverpool contract no harm with the winner as head coach Andoni Iraola got off to a winning Champions League start by beating Atletico Madrid 2-1 .

Mac Allister expressed his frustration at not being offered a new deal on the eve of Wednesday’s match, but responded by blasting home from the edge of the box to cap Liverpool’s comeback.

Marcos Llorente had given Atletico an early lead before Dominik Szoboszlai levelled the score before half-time.

Victory came at a cost for the Reds, though, as new signing Bradley Barcola limped off with a calf injury.

For the first time three players who cost in excess of 100 million pounds ($135m) were named in the same side as Barcola made his Anfield debut alongside Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz in the Liverpool attack.

Isak fired just wide after a purposeful break by Szoboszlai in an energetic start by Liverpool in the first Champions League game of Iraola’s career.

But in their desperation to pour forward, the Reds left themselves wide open to the counterattack.

Atletico were humbled 3-0 by Athletic Bilbao on Saturday to cap an underwhelming start to the season by Diego Simeone’s men.

Julian Alvarez’s future has cast a cloud over Atletico on and off the field for the past few months after his desire for a move to Barcelona was steadfastly rejected by the club’s hierarchy.

The Argentinian was handed his first start of the season and cut open the Liverpool defence for the opening goal.

Llorente – who named his dog Anfield after scoring twice in Atletico’s last 16 win over Liverpool in 2020 – raced onto Alvarez’s pass to score his fifth goal in three visits to Anfield with the Spanish side.

Only a brilliant save by Alisson Becker denied Alvarez from long range before the Liverpool fightback began.

Barcola twice should have marked his first chance to impress his new fanbase with a goal.

The French winger, whose transfer from Paris Saint-Germain could cost Liverpool up to 123 million pounds ($166m), failed to squeeze the ball past Jan Oblak with just the giant Slovenian to beat.

However, Liverpool kept the attack alive and Ronald Araujo’s flick teed up Szoboszlai to find the bottom corner on 40 minutes.

Barcola missed an even better chance for his first Liverpool goal when he fired wide after being played in by Wirtz early in the second half.

Again, though, the reprieve was brief for the visitors.

Mac Allister had been linked with a move to Atletico during the transfer window and expressed his sadness at not being offered a new contract by Liverpool, while Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have agreed new deals in recent months.

The Argentinian international arrowed in a shot from outside the box on his weaker left foot and celebrated wildly in front of the Kop.

Liverpool’s joy was short-lived as Barcola pulled up holding his calf before the hour mark in what Iraola will hope is not a serious setback.

Iraola will be much happier with his side’s defensive display in the second half.

Alvarez fired too close to Alisson with one of the visitors’s few clear sights of goal.

A last-ditch challenge by Robin Le Normand denied Isak a third goal to round off a fine night for Liverpool.

But Iraola was able to celebrate his first statement win since taking charge.

Szoboszlai was awarded player of the match and told TNT Sports that it was a very even match.

“I am very happy to be back, these nights are always special and after a setback we came back in a good game,” he said.

“It was ups and downs all the time, they are good team, I think we have a quite good team as well. It was a 50/51.”

images.caption: Alexis Mac Allister scores Liverpool's winning goal in Wednesday's match against Atletico Madrid [Jason Cairnduff/Action Images via Reuters]

articles.title: Manchester United vs Sabah: UEFA Champions League – preview, team news
articles.summary: Man Utd have taken four points from their first four Premier League games, but Michael Carrick says team ready to rise.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick believes Manchester United are strong enough to compete with Europe’s best on their return to the Champions League for the first time in three years.

Carrick earned his position as permanent United boss after leading the Red Devils to third place in English football’s Premier League in his interim spell last season.

Having secured a place in Europe’s elite club competition, United kick off their league phase campaign on Thursday when they face Azerbaijani champions Sabah at Old Trafford in Manchester.

“It’s a magical competition. It’s where we all want to be. When you’re out of it, you realise how special it is, and when you’re in it, you want to make the most of it,” Carrick told reporters on Wednesday.

“I think we’ve all seen some special, special nights and felt some special things in this competition over the years. It’s the best competition to challenge yourself and to push against the best.

“We’re delighted to be here, but we’re not here to just enjoy the occasion. We’re here to do business and go as far as we possibly can.”

In two of their last three appearances in the Champions League, the three-time European champions have crashed out at the group stage, and they have not progressed beyond the last 16 since 2019.

United have also made a slow start to the Premier League season, taking just four points from fixtures against Hull, Ipswich and Everton.

However, many of their better performances under Carrick have come against stronger opposition.

United beat Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea in the second half of last season.

“I think we’re capable of doing some really good things in this competition, and going further down the line,” Carrick said.

“Certainly not getting ahead of ourselves because some part of it is a new experience for some of the players.

“But the boys are used to playing European football for the most part in different competitions, and we’ll take that forward and we’ve got a squad that’s strong enough to compete.”

In contrast to the record-setting spending by many of their Premier League rivals, United were only able to strengthen their midfield in the transfer window.

United benefitted last season from only playing 40 games – their lowest total since the 1914-15 campaign.

Carrick, though, said his players had to embrace the challenge of a heavier workload.

“We play Thursday, Sunday, Wednesday and it’s what we’re here for. It’s about managing the group and having trust in everyone able to play,” he said.

Benjamin Sesko is in contention for his first start of the season after coming off the bench to score in Sunday’s 2-2 draw at Everton.

Carrick confirmed Matthijs de Ligt is also nearing a comeback after nearly a year out with a back injury.

images.caption: Michael Carrick is in his first full football season as Manchester United's manager [Jon Super/Reuters]

articles.title: Misfiring Arsenal beat Napoli with Odegaard stunner in Champions League
articles.summary: Arsenal dominated play but needed a screamer from Martin Odegaard to seal three points in Napoli to open league phase.
articles.body:
Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard’s sensational late strike broke stern Napoli resistance as the English champions began their bid for Champions League glory with a hard-fought 1-0 win in Naples on Wednesday.

Mikel Arteta’s side, who lost to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties in last season’s final, spurned several glorious chances against the well-drilled hosts before Odegaard lashed a shot off the post and in from the edge of the area with 15 minutes to go.

It continued a perfect start to the campaign for Arsenal, who began their Premier League title defence with three wins in a row before condemning Massimiliano Allegri’s team to a third consecutive defeat.

Arsenal’s next European test comes at home against Lille on Tuesday, October 13. Napoli travel to Villarreal on the same day as they look to bounce back.

Injuries to Scott McTominay and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa forced Allegri into a midfield reshuffle, with Kevin De Bruyne and Billy Gilmour coming in. Left-back Mathias Olivera was also selected after the hosts had let a two-goal lead slip to lose 3-2 away to Inter Milan on Saturday.

Arteta made four changes from Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Chelsea on Sunday, with Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres earning their first starts of the season.

The hosts set out to soak up pressure and frustrate last season’s runners-up, who struggled to break the low block early on and were almost caught out at the other end when De Bruyne and Matteo Politano both called goalkeeper David Raya into action.

Arsenal carved out a big chance midway through the first half when Merino’s header from 8 yards out was pushed over the bar by Alex Meret.

The Gunners, who won all eight of their league phase games to kick-start their run to the final last season, continued to probe as Ben White produced a tame finish from a promising position before Meret scooped a Hincapie cross-shot off his line.

Rasmus Hojlund’s hold-up play was proving a useful weapon for Napoli on the counter, as Politano forced another save from Raya.

But it was Arsenal who ended the first half feeling they should have been in front, after Saka was played through on goal and had only the keeper to beat, only to lift a poor finish over the bar.

Napoli were forced into a goalkeeper change during the interval, with Vanja Milinkovic-Savic replacing the injured Meret, but Arsenal picked up where they left off as Hincapie wasted another good chance by scooping his shot over from 5 yards.

Arsenal continued to knock at the door to no avail until the 75th minute, when in-form Odegaard smashed an unstoppable shot in off the post from the edge of the area, just three days after scoring a winning strike against Chelsea.

The visitors had a huge chance to settle it with five minutes to go when Noni Madueke had a shot charged down by Milinkovic-Savic before fellow substitute Christos Tzolis’s follow-up effort was blocked on the line.

They were almost made to pay when a neat passing move from Napoli left De Bruyne with space in the box, but the Belgian opted to play a ball across an empty 6-yard box instead of shooting.

Kai Havertz thought he had doubled the Gunners’ lead in stoppage time with a tap-in from Milinkovic-Savic’s parry, but the offside flag was up.

articles.title: Rangers 1-0 St Mirren: Bojan Miovski comes off bench to score stoppage-time winner and extend winning run
articles.summary: Report as Bojan Miovski's stoppage-time dink snatched victory after St Mirren had passed up the game's biggest chance through Fraser Taylor; Rangers move above St Mirren in the Scottish Premiership
articles.body:
The substitute raced onto Ryan Naderi's flick-on from Ivor Pandur's long ball before lifting a delightful lob over the goalkeeper to send Ibrox wild after a drab 90 minutes.

It looked for all the world that Derek McInnes' side were set to be frustrated after struggling to break down a resolute St Mirren side who packed a punch of their own.

St Mirren could easily have taken all three points, having created the clearest chance of the game when Fraser Taylor was sent through one-on-one with Pandur.

In a miss that would prove costly, the forward had time to pick his spot, but his effort was too close to the Rangers goalkeeper, who made a comfortable save.

The victory moves Rangers above St Mirren and into second in the Scottish Premiership, with the visitors suffering a second consecutive league defeat after their 2-1 loss to Celtic last time out.

Rangers had to cope without captain and striker Lawrence Shankland, who missed out through injury, with Ryan Naderi starting in his place.

But it was another substitute who provided the decisive moment as Miovski produced a composed finish to ensure Rangers' momentum under McInnes continues.

Rangers turn their attention to a huge double-header against Celtic, with the sides first meeting in the League Cup quarter-finals before renewing hostilities in the Scottish Premiership at Parkhead.

17: BIG SAVE! Raskin denied! He meets a Bouanani cross from the right and nods towards goal but Jacob Chapman produces a super stop.

22: CHAPMAN DOUBLE SAVE! The St Mirren stopper is in inspired form. He first gets down to a Gassama strike from the edge of the area. Bouanani rushes in to gobble up the rebound but that's saved too!

66: BIG MISS! How has Taylor missed!???? Pandur comes up on top in a one-on-one as Fraser spurns the chance of the game.

90+1: GOAL! Naderi flicks on a long ball into Miovski's path, who's then one-on-one with Chapman. The St Mirren 'keeper rushes out and is beaten with a cute dink.

McInnes: We'd like to win with more ease but we are making good steps

Rangers boss Derek McInnes speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm very relieved. The way we moved the ball, the aggression and the chances we created, we should have done so much better. For an hour I was really pleased with the performance. Then for 20 to 25 minutes we were guilty of so many bad decisions, but we found a way to win.

"I couldn't be more pleased with my players for their perseverance and sheer will to keep going. When you get a late winner, it illustrates the strength, fitness and character of the team.

"Four wins out of four; I think it's six out of seven. We're making good steps but we'd like to be able to win a bit more comfortably and at more ease.

"As long as we're winning, it's a step towards hopefully getting more complete performances."

On Bojan Miovski : "I'm delighted for him. He just keeps going, trains with motivation, does the right things and had a lovely, calm finish when we needed calmness and quality."

McLeish: We played like monsters tonight - we deserved at least a point

St Mirren boss Craig McLeish speaking to Sky Sports:

"I was delighted with how we played tonight; we asked them to be brave and they stuck to what we've been doing. Chapman had to make some great saves; we defended well but could have carried a bit more threat.

"It felt like we deserved at least a point but you don't always get what you deserve. There are no excuses about four games in 12 days; we played like monsters tonight.

"We've had some moments like those that have gone our way. These things even themselves out and Fraser Taylor was fantastic tonight. I'm just so proud of the group and we have to keep going.

"I don't want this to come across the wrong way but our season can't be defined by picking up a point away at Ibrox. If we play like we did tonight, then we should keep picking up more points throughout the season."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: El Cholo dio la sorpresa en Anfield al alinear de salida a Julián Alvarez, un paso hacia su rehabilitación. Y salió bien. Su actuación fue convincente: le metió a Llorente el pase para su quinto gol en Anfield (que marcó con empaque de delantero centro grande), le sacó a Alisson su mejor parada del partido y jugó en general bien, con solidaridad y sentido práctico. Su rostro aún es taciturno, pero de su juego ayer no puede haber queja. Pena que eso no sirvió para sacar un resultado útil en Liverpool, a pesar del buen inicio, pues el de Llorente fue el primer gol del partido. Pero luego, el fútbol potente y áspero del Liverpool, que sintetiza muy bien la figura bronca y rocosa de Mac Allister, le doblegó. Al Atlético le costó salir y transitar, digamos que en el forcejeo estuvo siempre un punto por detrás. El Cholo movió el equipo en busca de refrescarlo, pero también el Liverpool, con lo que finalmente ganó el encuentro con un apretado pero merecido 2-1. Lo de Julián Alvarez va entrando en agujas, pero hay alguna cosa preocupante, en especial las impresiones que viene dando Grimaldo. Al Atleti le espera un arranque de grupo difícil, habrá que tener paciencia. Lo de Anfield estuvo precedido del partido del Spotify, que vino a confirmarnos que en el Barça de estos días siempre es Nochebuena. Ya son 22 goles en cinco partidos oficiales, una sucesión de exhibiciones de fútbol de ataque. Calidad más calidad da más calidad y así indefinidamente. De esos 22 goles, 7 corresponden a Raphinha, ese nueve móvil, solución improvisada por la fuerza de las circunstancias. Y hasta hubo un rato para Gabriel Jesus, que se cobró el quinto gol, al que sumó un cabezazo que botó en la cara alta del larguero. En la feliz noche, Lamine se apuntó un gol de golpe franco gracias, todo hay que decirlo, a una barrera transparente, pero que vendrá a apuntalar el humor del joven ‘crack’. El Barça tiene tantos que juegan tan bien que resulta difícil hacerse un hueco a jugadores de tanto vuelo como Olmo y el combativo Gavi, campeones del mundo vigentes.

articles.title: Charlton 0-0 QPR: Hoops miss chance to move top of Championship following goalless draw at The Valley
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Charlton and QPR; the visitors had an opportunity to move top of the table but were forced to settle for a point
articles.body:
The R's knew a third straight away victory would take them to the summit but they were unable to produce a clinical finish at The Valley to back up some impressive approach play.

Both sides were looking to bounce back from their first league losses of the season at the weekend.

There was a big call by the officials on 39 minutes as Tyreece Campbell finished smartly from Oliver Skipp's incisive through pass. The goal was ruled offside but it looked a razor-fine decision whether the in-form attacker was just behind R's centre-back Ronnie Edwards at the key moment the ball was released by Leicester loanee Skipp, making his home debut.

"We scored the only goal of the game. I am sick of it. On the weekend, I had to put up with a performance from an individual that was beyond the realm of belief," Charlton boss Nathan Jones told Sky Sports after the game.

"Tonight, he had one decision to make and he gave offside. The goal is a great goal and a great counter-attack. It is onside and has cost us three points. The arrogance of the linesman is mental. He has looked at me like I have volleyed his cat."

The only effort on target came from a cheeky backheel finish by Rumarn Burrell from Vale's low cross but Okonkwo dropped to claim cleanly.

Charlton finished the half strongly with QPR captain Jimmy Dunne heading away a dangerous Campbell cross and referee Tom Nield ignored appeals for a penalty when Ivan Mesik went down under an awkward challenge by Cirkin.

QPR continued to dictate possession once the action resumed, despite yet another injury, captain Jimmy Dunne going off in the 47th minute.

Charlton centre-back Tyler Bindon was indebted to Okonkwo for a fine stop with his legs from Paul Smyth in the 62nd minute after losing the ball in a dangerous area - it proved to be the clearest scoring chance of the evening.

A sliding Burrell just failed to make a connection on substitute Amadou Mbengue's cross from six yards out as Charlton continued to struggle to get any kind of foothold in the contest.

There were fresh and fruitless spot-kick appeals from the hosts for a potential handball by Mbengue from a Rankin-Costello shot while Cirkin evaded any punishment for pulling back Karlan Grant to halt a dangerous home attack.

Charlton boss Nathan Jones speaking to Sky Sports:

"We scored the only goal of the game. I am sick of it. On the weekend, I had to put up with a performance from an individual that was beyond the realm of belief.

"Tonight, he had one decision to make and he gave offside. The goal is a great goal and a great counter-attack. It is onside and has cost us three points. The arrogance of the linesman is mental. He has looked at me like I have volleyed his cat.

"He is looking at me as if I have done something; he has made the biggest error of the night and has cost us the game. Our goalkeeper has had to make one save and we scored the one goal.

"That is the difference, I am proud of my team and it was a tough game."

"We were very, very dominant throughout the game - both halves.

"We had a lot of control and a lot of possession. But in the last 20 metres we didn't create enough big, big chances - even if we had a big one with Smythy in the second half.

"It is a mix of feelings after this game. I'm very satisfied with the way we played and the control we had, even if we are missing probably seven, eight or nine players - we kept our ability to be dominant.

"It is not an easy place here, I don't remember the last time that a team came here and was so dominant like this against Charlton. We didn't concede anything and that is a good sign.

"We know we have to improve a lot in the last third. We have to work on our patterns and continue to develop them, but we also need to find some players able to win some one-v-ones.

"I think we did well today. We collect a point, it's probably not enough based on the domination we had, but it is one more. If we are very disappointed to be third or fourth it is a good sign."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: St Johnstone 0-1 Celtic: Mika Baur nets first Hoops goal to make it six wins from six in the Scottish Premiership
articles.summary: Report as Celtic beat St Johnstone 1-0 at McDiarmid Park; Mika Baur scores his first Hoops goal to secure the victory; Martin O'Neill's side have won all six of their Scottish Premiership games this season
articles.body:
With a Europa League tie and an Old Firm cup and league double coming up, Martin O'Neill made five changes as Kasper Hogh returned from injury and Sam Johnstone took over in goal.

The on-loan keeper produced a huge save to deny Joel Cotterill - on his first St Johnstone start - as the hosts enjoyed the best of the chances.

The defending champions did take the lead after the break as Baur tapped in from Haissem Hassan's cross. The Egypt international was later denied his first goal with the ball ruled out of play before Hogh sent it back in for him to score.

The Premiership newcomers were unbeaten at McDiarmid Park this season and had chances to take something, but the champions held on to stay five points clear of second-placed Rangers at the top of the table.

Although far from their convincing best, the Hoops did enough to close out their 13th win in a row in total stretching back to the closing weeks of last season.

O'Neill's men are now five points clear of second-placed Rangers, who they also face in their next Premiership match a week on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: Derby 0-1 West Brom: Baggies move top of Championship with win at Pride Park despite Brayann Pereira red card
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Derby and West Brom at Pride Park; Aune Heggebo scored the only goal but West Brom were forced to hold on with 10 men for over an hour due to Brayann Pereira's red card
articles.body:
West Brom celebrated a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park after playing for more than an hour with 10 men.

The visitors went in front through Aune Heggebo only to have Brayann Pereira sent off on his debut for a second yellow card.

Pereira could have no complaints about the decision but his side showed determination and character to hold on despite almost constant second-half pressure.

Derby had their moments but created few clear-cut chances with the best falling to striker Lars-Jorgen Salvesen who headed over from eight yards.

There was one nervous moment deep in added time when the visitors survived a huge scramble on the edge of the six-yard box but they held on for a win that takes them top of the Championship table.

Derby made a confident start with Sam Szmodics causing problems but it was West Brom who took the lead in the 16th minute against the run of play.

A fast counter opened Derby up and Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipped in a low cross from the left which Heggebo finished at the near post.

After Derby's previous home game ended in defeat to Swansea, it was important they did not concede again and Heggebo headed a decent chance over from eight yards in the 25th minute.

But the visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute after he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor.

Pereira knew it was reckless given the earlier booking and pulled his shirt over his head as he left the pitch.

It opened the door for Derby, who went close in the 43rd minute when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in.

The start of the second half brought more problems for West Brom after Nolan Galves was injured in a challenge and had to be helped off the pitch.

Derby were turning up the heat and should have equalised in the 68th minute but Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward's cross.

That was the best chance Derby had created since the break, which was a testament to the way West Brom had defended under sustained pressure.

There was one last chance for Derby right at the end when Henrik Meister knocked the ball past Max O'Leary but Nat Phillips made a great clearance to sum up a performance full of grit and resolve.

"Obviously frustrated but I thought we started the game really well and even when we went a goal down I thought the whole of the first half was a real positive from my point of view.

"The lads did exactly what I wanted them to do and we had a couple of chances first half which we couldn't put away.

"Then in the second half West Brom defended really well and I'm disappointed that we couldn't break them down.

"We just need a bit more quality and the lads to step up and take responsibility for trying to make something happen. We got into some really good areas and we've got to keep working in that final third."

"I thought we were pretty poor for the first 20 or 30 minutes, we caused our own problems really.

"I think the sending off summed up our start really, we gave the ball away far too much and the one time we did string some passes together we scored.

"It was important we got to half time and sorted a few things out. We limited them to crosses coming in and heading from 12 yards, we defended the box really well with everyone putting their bodies on the line.

"That defensive unit of the whole team really when we were low was pretty impressive.

"I felt it from day one really, after last season to now, it's a credit to the lads and the new lads coming in and fitting in really well, hopefully that will spur us on."

articles.title: Chelsea 6-3 Leeds: Morgan Rogers-inspired Blues net SIX second-half goals in breathless comeback win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds at Stamford Bridge; Blues net six second-half goals with Cole Palmer, Danny Welbeck, Pedro Neto and Valentin Barco on target
articles.body:
The Blues found themselves two goals behind when Brenden Aaronson struck after 47 minutes to add to Tarik Muharemovic's opener, and it appeared Xabi Alonso's first real cup test would end in disappointment - despite the half-time introduction of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Reece James.

A Palmer penalty turned the game on its head suddenly after Pep Chavarria was caught by Dan James, but it was Rogers who inspired the comeback, making four of Chelsea's six goals.

Three of those assists - for Palmer's second, Neto's strike and the first of two for Danny Welbeck - came as Chelsea netted three times more in 12 minutes, including Welbeck's fourth which should have given them breathing space when he fired through Michael Zetterer's legs.

Not for the first time in Alonso's short reign however, chaos once again reigned over control as Leeds continued to create chances before Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled them back to within a goal with 15 minutes to go.

It was still uncertain that Chelsea had finally sealed their progress when Valentin Barco blasted them 5-3 up from close range from another Rogers assist, but they could finally rest easy in added time - and extinguish Leeds' commendable never-say-die attitude - when Welbeck nodded Barco's wildly mishit effort beyond Zetterer.

If there was ever a goal to sum up a game, this was it. Alonso was handed another clear indication of where his side remain lacking - but for now, chaos isn't serving them too badly.

Leeds head coach Daniel Farke on Sky Sports:

"We played with confidence, there was not even a chance for them, then the referee decided to give a penalty.

"Nobody was asking for it, all of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game."

Alonso: Always a risk making mass changes

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:

"There was so many changes. There was a risk. Things weren't going the way we planned, so we had to change. I take responsibility with the first half. The crowd were great, with the atmosphere [pushing the players on].

"I like that [the substitutes] were ready before the game. They knew they weren't starting and they were ready to make an impact.

"When you put together a team that hardly plays together, it is difficult to play at this level when [Leeds] are intense."

Palmer: It's a lot different under Alonso

Player of the match Cole Palmer on Sky Sports:

"You can see I'm enjoying it. Me and Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro, the attacking players.

"Not to say the defenders aren't - but it's a lot different.

"We've still got a bit to go, but we're getting results and that's the main thing."

articles.title: Napoli 0-1 Arsenal: Martin Odegaard goal clinches win for dominant Gunners in Champions League opener
articles.summary: Report as Martin Odegaard's goal ensures a 1-0 win for Arsenal in their Champions League league-phase opener against Napoli; Mikel Arteta's side dominated but wasted chances through Bukayo Saka, Mikel Merino and others before Odegaard's winner
articles.body:
The Gunners should have won by a bigger margin but missed a succession of chances before Odegaard crashed a low shot in off the post from the edge of the box following intricate build-up.

The goal, Odegaard's fourth in five games this season, ensured a winning start for last season's runners-up in this competition but wasteful finishing made it harder than it should have been.

Arsenal attempted 26 shots, their most on record in a Champions League game, worth a whopping 4.05 expected goals but Mikel Merino and Bukayo Saka spurned their best chances of the first half before Piero Hincapie blazed over from close range in the second.

As it happened | Teams | Stats | Champions League scores

Odegaard's goal, fired in following a quick one-two with substitute Christos Tzolis, finally broke the deadlock but Noni Madueke, another substitute, missed a one-on-one chance with Tzolis's follow-up blocked on the line, leaving Arsenal to suffer a late scare.

Former Manchester City playmaker Kevin De Bruyne appeared well placed to equalise when put through for a rare Napoli chance in the final few minutes, but wasted the chance by opting to cross, ensuring Arsenal could celebrate a victorious start to their European campaign and a fifth straight win of the season in all competitions.

22 SAVE! Eberechi Eze heads a Saka cross back across goal but Merino's header is parried

29: SLICE! Arsenal create another great opening but Saka fails to connect properly with his shot in the centre of the box

45: MISS! Odegaard plays Saka through on goal but he fires wastefully over the bar

50: WASTE! Odegaard lifts the ball over the top to White, whose cross finds Hincapie but the defender somehow blasts over from six yards out

75: AT LAST! Arsenal finally score as a slick passing move ends with Odegaard firing a low shot into the corner

85 SAVE! Kai Havertz puts Noni Madueke through on the counter but his shot is saved before Tzolis sees his follow-up effort blocked

89: SCARE! De Bruyne looks well placed to equalise but chooses to cross instead of shoot and wastes the chance

Odegaard is a player in form. That much was clear from early in this game. The Arsenal captain oozed class and confidence, demanding the ball then finding the gaps in Napoli's defence and threading passes forward. Everything went through him.

His goal, brilliantly taken from the edge of the box after a 29-pass build-up, proved crucial. He now has four in five games this season, a stunning turnaround having only managed one in 36 last term. Odegaard, uninhibited by injuries, looks a different player.

But showing his team-mates how to finish was only one part of his performance. He also ended the game having had more touches, made more passes and created more chances than anyone else on the pitch. Napoli couldn't really get near him.

The scooped pass to release Ben White for the golden chance somehow spurned by Piero Hincapie was one of many examples of his ingenuity against the massed ranks of Napoli players but there were plenty of others. He played with freedom and flair.

"Martin is contributing goals," said Mikel Arteta after the game. "That is obviously impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players, to be decisive, and certainly he was that today." Arsenal continue to feel the benefits.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports:

"I don't know the amount of chances and situations we generated but the performance doesn't reflect the result. It should have been much bigger - in a really tough environment, a really tough opponent. I think the team was superb.

"The way we competed, attitude, courage, the way we imposed ourselves on the game, the quality we showed to break them down, which is very difficult to do. It was a shame because we missed so many big chances.

"That's great that a lot of very different players got in those situations. Any other day the result [score] would be different."

Arsenal have won their last 13 group-stage games in the Champions League, the second-longest run in the competition's history after Bayern Munich (17 between December 2020 and November 2023).

Arsenal have kept 20 clean sheets in 40 Champions League games under Mikel Arteta, four more than any other side since the start of 2023/24.

Arsenal's 26 shots against Napoli was their most on record (since 2003/04) in a single Champions League match, while it was also the most Napoli have ever faced in the competition.

There were 29 passes in the build-up to Arsenal's winner, their second-most on record (since 2003/04) for a Champions League goal (33 for Lucas Perez's second at Basel in December 2016).

articles.title: Napoli 0-1 Arsenal: Martin Odegaard looks back to his best for Gunners
articles.summary: Another Arsenal win, another Martin Odegaard goal - the Gunners captain looks back to his best, writes Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Arsenal were one game away from the dream double of Premier League and Champions League last season, even with the brilliance of Martin Odegaard diminished by injuries and indifferent form.

As they look to go one better than that fully merited first Premier League title in 24 years, Arsenal and manager Mikel Arteta will be thrilled to see the 27-year-old Norwegian starting the new campaign in the form of his life.

If they could win the title and only lose to Paris St-Germain on penalties in the Champions League final with Odegaard in those reduced circumstances, what can Arsenal achieve with their captain already stamping his authority so significantly domestically and in Europe?

Arsenal dominated Napoli in the opening game of their Champions League campaign, but it still took Odegaard to make the decisive contribution with a stunning left-foot strike 15 minutes from time to secure a 1-0 win.

It seems, with Odegaard in this form, Arsenal can overcome every test to make anything possible for Arteta's team.

Odegaard was troubled by knee and shoulder injuries last season, restricting him to only 36 games in all competitions, scoring just one goal with seven assists. He only played in 24 Premier League matches as Arsenal finally lifted the crown.

He showed signs of a revival as Norway reached the World Cup quarter-final, losing to England, but has moved on to a different level in the opening phase of this season.

Odegaard hits Arsenal winner to sink Napoli - report & ratings

Odegaard gave a flavour of what was to come in the Community Shield win against Manchester City in Cardiff with an audacious final goal in Arsenal 's 3-0 win, sitting down keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before passing the ball into an empty net.

He scored in the 3-0 victory against Coventry City , also scoring the winner as Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 at Emirates Stadium to maintain their 100% start.

Odegaard scored after a perfectly timed, intelligent run into the box that allowed him to step on to Kai Havertz's clever dummy before sending an emphatic finish past Chelsea keeper Emiliano Martinez.

This, and his winner in Naples, was the work of a lavishly gifted player finally operating at the peak of his powers once more, fully fit and playing in a team overflowing with the confidence and self-belief long-awaited success has given them.

It was a win Arsenal needed, because they face some tough Champions League assignments on the road ahead, such as a home game with Real Madrid and a visit to Bayern Munich.

The manner in which they patiently broke down Napoli's resistance, with the Serie A side utilising a defensive shield straight from veteran coach Max Allegri's well-thumbed playbook, showed calmness and maturity.

In every act this season, Arsenal already look like a side ready to build on their achievements of last term.

'When Odegaard is at his best, Arsenal are at their best'

Odegaard, as manager Arteta hinted, is almost playing like someone with something to prove, knowing himself that while Arsenal had a season of glory last time out, his personal contribution was not what he expected from himself.

Former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, a pundit on Wednesday's Match of the Day, said Odegaard "will want to have a bigger impact on the team this season".

"They have got unfinished business in the Champions League," said Onuoha. "He wants to be the first captain of Arsenal to lift that trophy.

"You would not back against them winning it based on what we've seen them do in this competition in the past two seasons, but he 100% takes Arsenal to a different level when he is on form and playing like this.

"That's the way it should be as well. I think when he is at his best, Arsenal are at their best.

"I think there have been times when he's not been at his best and as a team they can still look good and win games, but the best version of Arsenal in my opinion comes when Odegaard is pulling the strings, because so many other players will be involved in the way they attack, and the way they attack will look different at certain points."

Odegaard caps dominant Arsenal performance

This time around, Odegaard looks smooth as silk – and it is no coincidence Arsenal look exactly the same.

"This is what we need: players with that mindset to decide the game, to play with that personality and keep taking risks," said Arteta. "He is getting into those positions much more in recent games. It was an incredible goal."

In Naples, Odegaard not only settled the game but set the tone, working tirelessly as the perfect of example of leadership as well as being the match winner.

" Arsenal have obviously looked good at the start of the season and he has been a big reason for that," added Onuoha. "Some of his creativity, especially on the right-hand side, has been excellent.

"He looks after the ball so well. He is always looking for that pass to be able to create opportunities and he even does the defensive work as well."

Odegaard succeeded where other team-mates failed, Arsenal missing several clear-cut opportunities before he struck.

Arsenal 's superiority was illustrated by having 26 shots, their most in a single Champions League match since records started being kept in 2003-04. It was also the most Napoli have faced in that time.

"Martin is contributing with goals that are impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players, being decisive," said Arteta. "We should have done it in a different way because of the amount of chances we created."

The Champions League has proved elusive for Arsenal , with finals lost to Barcelona in 2006 and to PSG last season.

It remains their Holy Grail – but if Odegaard maintains his brilliant form then their chances of crossing a so far insurmountable barrier will increase hugely.

articles.title: Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid: Alexis Mac Allister does talking on pitch
articles.summary: After saying he was "very sad" at the lack of a contract offer from Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister proved his worth against Atletico Madrid.
articles.body:
The sheer ferocity of the strike to beat Jan Oblak was one thing, but the raw emotion shown by Alexis Mac Allister as he grabbed the Liverpool badge on his shirt and celebrated in front of the Kop told you all that you needed to know.

Just a day earlier, Mac Allister had spoken with a different kind of emotion inside the press room at Anfield as he expressed his sadness at Liverpool not offering him a new contract during the summer .

The Argentine, who is currently contracted until 2028, spoke passionately about his love for the club and the city and how he didn't feel like he had anything to prove - but there was an admittance that he needed to show the level he knew he could perform at.

Thankfully for Andoni Iraola and Liverpool , Mac Allister did just that by letting his football do the talking in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid.

From the outset against Diego Simeone's side, the midfielder seemed like a man on a mission. He blazed over early on from outside the box then picked up a booking just before the half-hour mark. Seeing Simeone wave an imaginary yellow card when he wanted a second booking for his compatriot just before half-time told a story in itself.

Simeone could only watch on when Mac Allister's left foot connected with the ball from outside the box and leave a diving Oblak with no chance - turning the game on its head after Marcos Llorente's opening goal and Dominik Szoboszlai's equaliser.

It wasn't quite like the strike that produced an actual seismic event - reaching a peak magnitude of 1.74 on the Richter scale - when Mac Allister found the top corner against Tottenham in 2025 on the day Liverpool won the Premier League, but it was more than good enough to beat one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

Mac Allister scores winner as Liverpool beat Atletico Madrid - report and ratings

Mac Allister 'sad' at no Liverpool contract offer

And it was certainly what Iraola and the Anfield hierarchy would have wanted to see after a below-par campaign from Mac Allister last season.

The understanding is that they were of the belief that Mac Allister's performances did not warrant the offer of fresh terms.

But if he can carry on like this, then it will be a question of when rather than if that offer is made for whoever replaces Richard Hughes - even if Mac Allister said he didn't know if his goal would boost his chances of a new contract.

"It was a lovely goal from Alexis and a lovely goal from Dominik Szoboszlai. It is good the midfielders can add goals," said Iraola, who smartly navigated a question about Mac Allister's future.

"We have midfielders that naturally they are going to arrive to the box - it is inside them and it is good we can also benefit offensively."

Former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson said on BBC Radio 5 Live it was "exactly what Mac Allister needed to do".

"If you don't get offered a new contract there's a reason, so what do you do? You go out and earn it," said Robinson.

"You work hard, you play to your level and he did that. He put himself about and popped up with a wonderful strike."

Five of Mac Allister's 20 goals for Liverpool in all competitions have now come from outside the penalty area.

Steven Gerrard knows more than most about playing in midfield and scoring from distance for Liverpool and he described Mac Allister's performance as "outstanding".

"Let your football do the talking," said Gerrard on TNT Sports. "Consistency, top performance, show your experience. Show you're a top international. This club will reward you."

Mac Allister himself said how it was a "positive step" for Liverpool as they won for the first time at Anfield this season on what was Iraola's debut as a manager in the Champions League.

"It was a good comeback," said Mac Allister on TNT Sports. "Overall, it was a good performance. Now we have to think about the next one.

"Before the game we spoke about the beginning of the first half and second half. I liked the mentality.

"I think we showed desire today. We got the fans behind us and that's really important when you play at Anfield. A positive step for us."

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock said Mac Allister just needed to be put into a system that suits him to get the best out of him.

"I don't think he has to show his importance to Liverpool , I think everyone knows the qualities he has got anyway," said Warnock, who was a pundit on Wednesday's Match of the Day.

"I think there will be a lot of talk about him because of what has gone on in the past few days, but I think Liverpool fans were already asking why hasn't he been offered a new contract when other players have.

"To come out and talk about a contract situation like he did, a couple of days before a game, and to be able to back it up the way he did with a good performance is important - but it is over the course of the season, where his performances are important because if he wants a contract and he thinks he deserves a contract then if his performances are good, he will get one.

"We all know the qualities that he has got - he is a World Cup winner, a Premier League winner, we know that he's a very good player, it is just he has got to be put into the right system to make it work.

"At the moment Liverpool 's system is a little bit dysfunctional but it is starting to get better and he will get better because of that."

articles.title: Chelsea 6-3 Leeds: Xabi Alonso 'takes responsibility' as Palmer, Rogers and Welbeck rescue Blues in cup
articles.summary: Chelsea get the better of Leeds in a cup thriller, but Blues boss Xabi Alonso has food for thought after needing rescue act from his star substitutes.
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso watched his Chelsea team hit six goals in the second half against Leeds United but felt the need to "take responsibility" for the shaky start that came before the thrilling flurry.

Amid jubilation that followed the final whistle at Stamford Bridge, where Chelsea recovered from 2-0 down to progress as 6-3 winners in the Carabao Cup, it was easy to forget that Alonso's side were booed off at half-time.

Supporters witnessed arguably the worst first half of Alonso's short tenure to date, with Chelsea fortunate not to be further in arrears after the head coach made nine changes to his line-up.

The team's rhythm was disrupted. Leeds made eight changes themselves, but Daniel Farke's side took control and were threatening to surge into the fourth round.

Defender Tarik Muharemovic opened the scoring before Brenden Aaronson doubled Leeds ' lead shortly after the break.

Alonso had responded to Chelsea 's out-of-sorts start by making four substitutions at half-time. On came Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Reece James, and together they changed the game.

The sight of Palmer and Rogers warming up had gladdened the hearts of many, turning jeers to cheers. By the end of the night, Palmer had scored twice, fellow substitute Neto had also found the net, and Rogers left the field after helping to create four goals from open play in Chelsea 's remarkable turnaround.

However, speaking after the match, Alonso said he had made it "hard" for his players in the first place.

"I need to take my own blame and my own responsibility on the things that happen," he said. "I need to be able to help them better so they are not responsible, and after you need to react and think what's better for the team."

Alonso said the raft of substitutions he felt compelled to make should be considered "part of the game".

Chelsea come back to thump Leeds 6-3 in EFL Cup third round

Stars keep hopes alive for fringe players

For the Premier League's biggest clubs, this competition is usually an opportunity to blood youngsters and give fringe players valuable minutes.

However, only 35-year-old Danny Welbeck, who scored twice, emerged from the starters with a compelling case for more regular involvement.

Even Valentin Barco, despite scoring Chelsea 's fifth goal, was partly at fault for Leeds ' second and was among several players who repeatedly surrendered possession during a difficult first half.

Young attackers Estevao Willian and Jamie Gittens suffered the disappointment of being substituted at half-time, while £40m signing Geovany Quenda, who joined from Sporting, did not add to his solitary substitute appearance for the club as he watched from the bench.

Midfielder Reggie Watson, making his debut at the age of 16, was also withdrawn at the break after being booked.

Alonso later said he would not take a "cynical" view as some on the outside might about the difference in level between his proven stars and Chelsea 's back-up options.

He added: "I know that probably I have to take the right decisions for them to show their best level, so it's something that I will analyse and learn from today."

Nevertheless, reaching the fourth round is important for Chelsea .

It is not only about preserving their hopes of silverware in a season without European football, but Chelsea are also a club that need as many competitive fixtures as possible.

They have a 27-man squad, supported by a strong academy pipeline, and these matches are vital for keeping a large group of players engaged throughout the campaign.

There is an irony, then, that Palmer, Rogers and Chelsea 's other established stars may have secured future opportunities for the very fringe players whose performances had put the club's EFL Cup campaign at risk.

articles.title: Prince William launches landmark suicide prevention toolkit for sport on World Suicide Prevention Day
articles.summary: Prince William to launch new suicide prevention toolkit for sport; Dame Kelly Holmes, Jill Scott, Gabby Logan, Campbell Hatton and Dame Laura Kenny among sporting figures backing initiative; FA, Premier League, British Cycling and Team GB committed to implementing toolkit
articles.body:
The landmark event will take place at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool on World Suicide Prevention Day, September 10.

Dame Kelly Holmes, Gabby Logan, Campbell Hatton, Jill Scott and Dame Laura Kenny are among those joining the Prince of Wales at the launch of 'On Your Side' .

The toolkit, developed by The Royal Foundation in partnership with the British Standards Institution and mental health charity Chasing the Stigma, aims to turn suicide prevention into everyday practice across the sporting sector.

It will be available on Chasing the Stigma's Hub of Hope, the UK's largest mental health directory.

To mark the launch, The Royal Foundation has also produced a short film encouraging people to have the confidence to start a conversation about suicide.

The film features England captain Harry Kane, Formula 1 driver George Russell, two-weight world champion boxer Carl Frampton, GB international basketball player Kofi Josephs, Women's Rugby World Cup winner Rocky Clark, double world champion boxer, kickboxer and Muay Thai champion Ruqsana Begum and former elite jockey-turned-jockey coach George Baker.

The Football Association, Premier League, British Cycling and Team GB are among the major sporting organisations committing to implement the toolkit.

The FA, of which The Prince is patron, will commit to embedding the toolkit across its entire organisation, as well as its community and grassroots football network.

The Premier League and British Cycling will announce their commitment to prioritising suicide prevention across their organisations, while Team GB will use the resource with all athletes and staff.

More than a dozen other sports organisations have also signed up to become champions of the toolkit, committing to embedding practical, evidence-based suicide prevention techniques across their organisations.

The guidance includes advice on creating safe and supportive environments where people feel able to speak up and support others in distress, including appropriate language and conversation starters.

It also explains how to make suicide prevention part of everyday practice, educate people to spot warning signs and respond to someone in crisis, and put clear procedures in place for crisis situations and supporting people following a suicide.

At the centre of the resource is a five-step framework called GOALS, designed to help individuals start a conversation about suicide. It stands for:

The toolkit is designed for use across all sporting environments, from local clubs and academies to elite organisations, regardless of size, structure or level. It is relevant to everyone involved in sport, including players, coaches, staff, volunteers, families and spectators.

Research commissioned by The Royal Foundation found that the sports sector has the potential to be a powerful platform for suicide prevention, but is hampered by stigma - particularly among men and elite athletes - as well as gaps in skills, knowledge and resources.

The findings also showed strong goodwill and pockets of effective practice across sport, but that the sector's scale and diversity mean activity is often siloed, inconsistent and unevenly resourced. At grassroots level, many clubs lack clear guidance on how to recognise risk and respond appropriately.

During the event, representatives from across the sports ecosystem will also have the opportunity to share insights and reflections from their own organisations in a session hosted by Sue Gregory, CEO of Everton in the Community.

The initiative builds on the National Suicide Prevention Network, launched in autumn 2025 with more than £1m of funding from The Royal Foundation over an initial three-year period.

The network aims to deliver lasting change in how suicide is understood and prevented across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

The Prince and Princess of Wales and The Royal Foundation have made changing the conversation around mental health and suicide prevention a longstanding priority, with the aim of tackling stigma and helping people find the right support at the right time and in the right place.
